title: SLC6A1 and STXBP1: Questions Before Joining Forces

sentences.text: Given the disputed evidence in both disorders, are unstable or incorrectly folded proteins a strong enough shared basis for a joint project?
Does having one working gene copy that is not enough explain both groups well enough for joint research, given the disputed evidence in STXBP1?
Are the listed differences in GABA recycling for SLC6A1 and release of nerve signals for STXBP1 real biological differences or gaps in what has been studied?
How would disputed STXBP1 findings about altered proteins blocking working proteins, or sometimes doing too much, affect the case for studying both disorders together?
Do the entry rules and study schedule for Simons Searchlight suit families from both groups equally?
Do the entry rules and visit schedule for the phenylbutyrate study suit families from both groups equally?
Given the different mixes of gene changes, would ways of measuring progress developed for one disorder work for the other?
Are the listed differences in seizures, eyelid jerks, difficulty following movement sideways with the eyes, and brain dysfunction in infancy real differences or gaps in records?
What would need to change for the COMBINEDBrain / Across Matrix SLC6A1 natural history platform to include STXBP1 families?
Could Citizen Health, COMBINEDBrain Biorepository, or Simons Searchlight support a joint project using the records or samples they collect from both communities?
